evidence.mechanism: shot-02s: all celadon branch tips lit on khaki, with the flow arrow low on the left tick column; by shot-08s the top-centre crown turns dark slate as the arrow passes the 20 cm/s tick.
evidence.ambition: shot-08s: one line-drawn L-system tree with a faint halo and a tick-column dial, with no second layer, shading or simulation depth visible; shot-20s is the same single stroke style at smaller scale.
evidence.craft: shot-02s: cohesive khaki, celadon and slate palette with crisp thin strokes and clean mirrored symmetry; flaws are a small caption line at bottom-left and sparse wire-thin branches in the lower fan.
evidence.distinctness: shot-08s: slate-on-khaki mirrored tree with a dark crown is unlike last nights' apricot sand grid, dendrite type or cream Penrose tiling; shot-20s keeps that palette and form.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: centred colony with the dial already set at 2s; shot-20s shrinks to a margin-framed colony with the arrow back near the threshold, so the loop closes, but the crown change is subtle.

pairwise_justification: The median Penrose at 20s is a dense ochre and rust tiling filling the frame, while tonight at 20s is a sparse thin-line tree with a small dark crown; the median shows more visible development and material.

critique.change: Give the branches solid material at shot-02s: fill the lit shell with shaded or thickened tips instead of single strokes, and let the shielded crown darken those filled surfaces so the mechanism has a second visual layer to act on.
Make the stagnant zone a real interior pocket: at shot-08s darken the centre of the colony, not only the top crown, so the dark core reads inside the lit shell as the caption promises.
Give shot-20s a visibly different state from shot-02s, for example the dark core spreading into the lower fan or new khaki tips accreting at the edge, so the loop resolves with more than a rescale.
